Those objections don't really matter. A faithful copy of a macro-scale thing like a human brain is good enough to call meaningfully identical, or at least "the same". People get brain damage in car crashes, recover, and are "the same" people. The atoms are red herrings. Also, if there are two of you and they're the same, it doesn't matter at all which one came first, so the question isn't "why is it wrong to terminate my clone" but "why is it wrong to terminate one of me when there are two of me," and the question stands.

The multiverse bit (or infinite universe bit) doesn't have bearing on the problem either. This is a local problem for local effects.

Is it all about feelings? You feel OK about the idea of cloning yourself for this purpose, including tidying up by killing one of yourself afterward. Therefore your clone feels OK about it too.

If you're going into it thinking "I will hate this as a clone, and my non-clone self will coerce my clone self, and that's the plan because it gets the cleaning done," then the cleaning part becomes more difficult. I think in that case you're doing something irrational and morally wrong: you think really that even your clone should not be cleaning, that's why you hate the prospect of it.

The killing part would still be fine unless you say "I hate the thought of me being killed, but I'm fine with indistinguishable other-me, who is also me, being killed", which makes no sense.
